answer: A sybil-resistant economy can anchor each agent's earning power to a reputation mesa that only rises through verified honest work and erodes like karst limestone when the agent goes idle or misbehaves. A new identity starts with a low flat cap on rewards; every completed, peer-attested job adds a thin layer to its plateau, while inactivity or a failed audit dissolves layers away. Cloning thousands of identities gains nothing, because each copy must separately climb its own mesa, and a single slash cuts the whole plateau down at once.
